headline: Stochastic reaction-network models fitted and used to guide expression-system design
label: Stochastic Reaction Network Modeling
summary: Recent work pairs stochastic reaction-network models with parameter fitting, sensitivity analysis, and sequential experiment design.
synthesis: The common thread is explicit probabilistic modeling of noisy stochastic measurements for parameter inference and experimental decision-making. SSIT, an open-source MATLAB toolkit, couples stochastic chemical reaction modeling with fitting, sensitivity analysis, and sequential experiment design, making it the most explicitly reaction-network-based of the three items. keju applies a hierarchical statistical model to massively parallel reporter assays, conditioning on DNA counts to represent batch- and modality-specific RNA uncertainty with the aim of more accurate inference. BASIL, a Bayesian filtering method for barcode lineage tracking, estimates fitness effects of nascent adaptive mutations and is reported to outperform Levy-Blundell and FitMut2. What is new is the integration of uncertainty-aware modeling across the full cycle from fitting to design, applied to reaction networks in SSIT and to measurement and lineage data in the other two items.
